items.title: The Four Classes Give Rise to Karma — and the First Judge of the Dead

items.zh: 復次，於世間四姓生已，方乃發起順愛不愛五趣受業。從此以後，隨一有情由感雜染增上業故，生那洛迦中作靜息王。
items.en: Further, once the four classes had arisen in the world, beings then began to generate karma leading to desirable and undesirable rebirths across the five realms. From this point on, one being, through the dominant force of defiled karma, was reborn in hell as the Quiescence King.

items.zh: 從此無間，有那洛迦卒，猶如化生，及種種苦具，謂銅鐵等那洛迦火起。然後隨業有情於此受生，及生餘趣。

items.title: Small, Medium, and Great Chiliocosms — One Buddha-Field

items.zh: 如是百拘胝四大洲，百拘胝蘇迷盧，百拘胝六欲天，百拘胝梵世間，三千大千世界俱成俱壞。即此世界有其三種。一、小千界，謂千日月乃至梵世，總攝為一。二、中千界，謂千小千。三、大千界，謂千中千。合此名為三千大千世界。
items.en: Thus, a hundred koṭis of the four great continents, a hundred koṭis of Mount Sumeru, a hundred koṭis of the six desire-realm heavens, and a hundred koṭis of the Brahmā world all together form, and are destroyed together, as one great trichiliocosm. This world, moreover, is of three kinds. First, the small chiliocosm: a thousand suns and moons, up to a thousand Brahmā worlds, gathered together as one. Second, the medium chiliocosm: a thousand small chiliocosms. Third, the great chiliocosm: a thousand medium chiliocosms. Together, these are called a great trichiliocosm.

items.zh: 如是四方上下無邊無際三千世界，正壞正成。猶如天雨，注如車軸，無間無斷，其水連注，墮諸方分。如是世界遍諸方分，無邊無際，正壞正成。即此三千大千世界名一佛土。如來於中現成正覺，於無邊世界施作佛事。
items.en: Throughout the ten directions, boundless and without limit, trichiliocosms are, at any given moment, some being destroyed while others are being formed — just as when rain falls from the sky in an unbroken stream, thick as a cart's axle, pouring down ceaselessly on many places at once. So too do these worlds, spread throughout every direction, boundless and without limit, undergo destruction and formation without pause. This very trichiliocosm is called a single Buddha-field. It is within this field that the Tathāgata manifests the attainment of complete awakening, while carrying out the work of a Buddha throughout boundless worlds.

items.title: Five Realms, Four Kinds of Birth, Ten Units of Time

items.zh: 如是安立世界成已，於中五趣可得，謂那洛迦、傍生、餓鬼、人、天。及四生可得，謂卵生、胎生、濕生、化生。
items.en: Once the world has thus been established, five realms may be found within it: hell, the animal realm, the realm of hungry ghosts, the human realm, and the heavens. And four kinds of birth may be found: birth from an egg, birth from a womb, birth from moisture, and birth by transformation.

items.zh: 復有十種時分，謂時、年、月、半月、日、夜、剎那、怛剎那、臘縛、目呼剌多。
items.en: There are, further, ten units of time: the season, the year, the month, the half-month, the day, the night, the instant (kṣaṇa), the tat-kṣaṇa, the lava, and the muhūrta.

items.title: Ten Ways People Make Use of Wealth

items.zh: 復有七攝受事。復有十種身資具。復有十種受欲者，此如中阿笈摩說。復有
items.en: There are, further, seven things to be provided for; ten kinds of bodily requisites; and ten kinds of those who make use of desires, as explained in the Madhyama Āgama. First: one who seeks wealth unlawfully, and then neither uses it for oneself, nor supports others with it, nor gives it in acts of merit. Second: one who seeks wealth unlawfully, and uses it only for oneself, without supporting others or giving in acts of merit. Third: one who seeks wealth unlawfully, but uses it for oneself, supports others with it, and gives it in acts of merit. Fourth: one who seeks wealth both lawfully and unlawfully, and then neither uses it for oneself, nor supports others, nor gives in acts of merit.

Fifth: one who seeks wealth both lawfully and unlawfully, uses it for oneself, but neither supports others nor gives in acts of merit. Sixth: one who seeks wealth both lawfully and unlawfully, uses it for oneself, supports others, and gives it in acts of merit. Seventh: one who seeks wealth lawfully, and then neither uses it for oneself, nor supports others, nor gives in acts of merit. Eighth: one who seeks wealth lawfully, uses it for oneself, but neither supports others nor gives in acts of merit.

items.zh: 復有八世法，謂得、不得、若譽、若毀、稱、譏、苦、樂。
items.en: There are, further, eight worldly conditions: gain, loss, praise behind one's back, blame behind one's back, praise to one's face, mockery to one's face, suffering, and pleasure.

items.zh: 復有三品，謂怨、親、中。復有三種世事。復有三種語言。復有二十二種發憤。復有六十二種有情之類。又有八位。復有四種入胎。復有四種威儀。復有六種活命。復有六種守護。復有七種苦。復有七種慢。復有七種憍。復有四種言說。復有眾多言說句。

items.title: What "Destiny" Means, Across All Five Realms

items.zh: 云何那落迦趣？謂種果所攝那洛迦諸蘊，及順那洛迦受業。如那洛迦趣如是，傍生、餓鬼、人、天、如其所應盡當知。
items.en: What is the hell-destiny? It is the aggregates of hell, comprised of both seed and fruit, together with the karma that leads to experiencing rebirth in hell. As with the hell-destiny, so too with the animal, hungry-ghost, human, and heavenly destinies — each should be understood in the corresponding way.

items.title: The Four Kinds of Birth, Defined and Illustrated

items.zh: 云何卵生？謂諸有情破㲉而出。彼復云何？如鵞、雁、孔雀、鸚鵡、舍利鳥等。云何胎生？謂諸有情胎所纏裹，剖胎而出。彼復云何？如象、馬、牛、驢等。
items.en: What is birth from an egg? It is when beings emerge by breaking through a shell. What are these? Such as geese, wild geese, peacocks, parrots, and śārikā birds. What is birth from a womb? It is when beings, wrapped within a womb, emerge through the womb's opening. What are these? Such as elephants, horses, cattle, and donkeys.

items.zh: 云何濕生？謂諸有情隨因一種濕氣而生。彼復云何？如蟲、蝎、飛蛾等。云何化生？謂諸有情業增上故，具足六處而生，或復不具。彼復云何？如天、那洛迦全，及人、鬼、傍生一分。
items.en: What is birth from moisture? It is when beings arise dependent on some form of moisture. What are these? Such as worms, scorpions, and moths. What is birth by transformation? It is when beings, through the dominant force of karma, arise with the six sense-faculties complete, or else incomplete. What are these? Entirely so among the gods and in the hells, and in part among humans, hungry ghosts, and animals.

items.title: Six Kinds of Support for Life

items.zh: 云何六種依持？一、建立依持，謂最下風輪及水輪、地輪。令諸有情不墜下故起，是名依持。二、藏覆依持，謂屋宇等。為諸有情離流漏等所損故起，是名依持。彼屋宇等略有三種。或由造作，或不由造作，或宮殿化起。
items.en: What are the six kinds of support? First, the support of foundation: the lowest wheel of wind, together with the wheel of water and the wheel of earth, established so that beings do not fall through — this is called support. Second, the support of shelter: dwellings and the like, established so that beings are spared harm from rain, wind, and other such elements — this is called support. Such dwellings are, in brief, of three kinds: those that are built, those that arise without being built, and palaces that arise by transformation.

items.zh: 三、豐稔依持，為諸有情段食故起，是名依持。四、安隱依持，為諸有情離刀仗等所害故起，是名依持。五、日月依持，為諸有情見色故起，是名依持。六、食依持，謂四食。一、段食，二、觸食，三、意思食，四、識食。為諸有情任持身故起，是名依持。
items.en: Third, the support of abundance, established for the sake of beings' solid food — this is called support. Fourth, the support of security, established so that beings are spared harm from weapons and the like — this is called support. Fifth, the support of sun and moon, established so that beings can perceive form — this is called support. Sixth, the support of nourishment: the four kinds of food — solid food, contact, volition, and consciousness — established to sustain beings' bodies. This is called support.

items.title: Seven Things a Life Must Provide For

items.zh: 云何七種攝受事？一、自父母事，二、妻子事，三、奴婢僕使事，四、朋友官僚兄弟眷屬事，五、田宅邸肆事，六、福業事及方便作業事，七、庫藏事。
items.en: What are the seven things to be provided for? First, the matter of one's own parents. Second, the matter of one's wife and children. Third, the matter of servants and attendants. Fourth, the matter of friends, officials, brothers, and other relations. Fifth, the matter of fields, houses, residences, and shops. Sixth, the matter of meritorious deeds, and of the practical means needed to accomplish them. Seventh, the matter of one's stored wealth.

items.zh: 云何十種身資具？一、食，二、飲，三、乘，四、衣，五、莊嚴具，六、歌笑舞樂，七、香鬘塗末，八、什物之具，九、照明，十、男女受行。
items.en: What are the ten bodily requisites? First, food. Second, drink. Third, conveyance. Fourth, clothing. Fifth, ornaments. Sixth, song, laughter, dance, and music. Seventh, fragrance, garlands, and unguents. Eighth, household implements. Ninth, illumination. Tenth, the conduct of male and female.

blocks.text: The account of the world's formation ends with the first karma and the first judge of the dead, then widens to the scale of a whole Buddha-field. After that the treatise changes style: a long series of short numbered lists describing the conditions of life in the world we now inhabit (five realms, four births, ten units of time, the uses of wealth, the eight worldly winds, and the supports and requisites of life). Many of these lists recur throughout Buddhist literature, so they are worth recognising.

Untranslated passages: 0288a11–a14 (immediately after Yama's rebirth, hell-wardens appear as if by transformation, with the instruments of torment and the fires of hell, and only then are beings born there according to their karma); 0288a27 ("there are, further, six kinds of support"); and 0288b03–b09, a summary list of the topics that follow (the three groups of enemy, friend, and neutral; three worldly affairs; three kinds of speech; twenty-two occasions for anger; sixty-two kinds of beings; eight stages; four ways of entering the womb; four postures; six livelihoods; six protections; seven sufferings; seven conceits; and more).

subs.head: The four classes make karma, and the Quiescence King

blocks.text: Once the four social classes exist, beings make wholesome and unwholesome karma, and so the hells come into being. The first being reborn there, "through the dominant force of defiled karma", is called the **Quiescence King** (靜息王). Venerable Miào Jìng identifies him as **King Yama** (閻羅王): he tells those who come before him, "Do no more evil!", hence the name. Master Cháng Bǎi stresses that Yama is not a fixed cosmic office; he is a being who is there because of his own karma. Even the judge of the dead is inside the system of cause and effect.

A thousand worlds, each with its sun, moon, Sumeru, continents, and heavens up to Brahmā, make a small chiliocosm; a thousand of those make a medium one; a thousand of those make a great one. Venerable Miào Jìng: "three thousand" in 三千大千世界 refers to the three thousandfold steps; it is a single great chiliocosm, not three thousand worlds. Kuījī reckons the "hundred koṭis" of continents here as a hundred million, a koṭi being a million in this text.
"This very trichiliocosm is called a single **Buddha-field** (佛土)." In it one Tathāgata manifests complete awakening, while carrying out a Buddha's work throughout boundless worlds.

subs.head: Five realms, four births, ten units of time

blocks.text: The world contains the five realms (hell, animals, hungry ghosts, humans, gods) and the **four kinds of birth** (四生): from an egg, from a womb, from moisture, and by transformation. Transformation birth needs nothing but the being's own karma, so it is the only kind among gods and hell-beings, and occurs only in part among humans, ghosts, and animals. Venerable Miào Jìng adds that transformation-born beings with "incomplete" faculties are those of the formless realm, who have no material faculties at all. Time is measured in ten units from the moment upwards.

subs.head: Ten ways of using wealth; eight worldly winds

blocks.text: Quoting the *Madhyama Āgama*, the treatise grades those who "make use of desires", from one who gets wealth unlawfully and neither enjoys it nor shares it, up to the tenth and best: one who seeks it lawfully, uses it, supports others, makes offerings, and "understands renunciation in making use of it". Master Cháng Bǎi points out that the ninth and tenth differ only in that understanding; generosity without insight into renunciation still falls short.

The **eight worldly winds** (八世法) are gain and loss, slander and praise behind one's back (毀、譽), praise and reproach to one's face (稱、譏), pleasure and pain. Venerable Miào Jìng's distinction between the two pairs of praise and blame is one Ru-Yi's translation also follows.

A being needs **six supports** (from the wheel of wind beneath us to shelter, clothing, sun and moon, and food); seven things a life must provide for; ten bodily requisites (food, drink, conveyance, clothing, ornaments, ointments, garlands, household implements, lamps, and a place to live; Venerable Miào Jìng notes that 什 in 什物 means "all sorts of things", not "ten").

Among the supports is the classical list of the **four nutriments** (四食): solid food, contact, volition, and **consciousness**. Both teachers identify consciousness-as-food with the ālayavijñāna: even with food, contact, and volition, the body lives only while the ālayavijñāna holds it, the same point we met on Day 4 with fainting and on Day 6 with the kalala.

quiz.q: The treatise says one being was reborn in hell as the "Quiescence King." According to Venerable Miào Jìng, who is this, and why the name?
options: an emanation of the Buddha
a king of the heavens
a god who never errs
he is King Yama; he admonishes those who come to suffer there, "Do no more evil," hence "Quiescence King" — and he himself is there because of his own defiled karma
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "King Yama — when those who are to suffer come to him, he tells them, 'Do no more evil!' Because he does this, he is called the Quiescence King." The text says he was reborn in hell "through the dominant force of defiled karma." Master Cháng Bǎi: it is not a fixed cosmic office but a role taken by whoever's karma qualifies; his lecture adds that after judging others he too must suffer, so he also wishes to practise.

quiz.q: Is a "great trichiliocosm" (三千大千世界) three thousand worlds? According to Venerable Miào Jìng —
options: yes, exactly three thousand
it is three thousand great chiliocosms
it is three worlds

no — a thousand worlds make a small chiliocosm, a thousand of those a medium, a thousand of those a great; "three thousand" refers to the three thousandfold steps, and it is really one great chiliocosm
quiz.why: "First, the small chiliocosm: a thousand suns and moons, up to a thousand Brahmā worlds, gathered together as one. Second, the medium chiliocosm: a thousand small chiliocosms. Third, the great chiliocosm: a thousand medium chiliocosms. Together, these are called a great trichiliocosm." Venerable Miào Jìng: "A small thousand, a medium thousand, a great thousand — that's why it is called a 'three-thousand great-thousand world.' It is really one great chiliocosm." One passage of Master Cháng Bǎi's lecture adds the three together, a common misunderstanding (as are A and B).

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what is "a single Buddha-field," and what does the Tathāgata do there?
options: one set of four continents
one small chiliocosm
one great trichiliocosm; within it the Tathāgata manifests complete awakening, while carrying out a Buddha's work throughout boundless worlds
all worlds in the ten directions
quiz.why: "This very trichiliocosm is called a single Buddha-field. It is within this field that the Tathāgata manifests the attainment of complete awakening, while carrying out the work of a Buddha throughout boundless worlds." The *Pixunji*: in one great trichiliocosm only one Tathāgata appears, never a second. Venerable Miào Jìng: a Buddha can act throughout countless worlds, but to manifest Buddhahood there is only one Buddha per world-system. D confuses the reach of a Buddha's work with the extent of a Buddha-field.

quiz.q: Once the world is established, the treatise says four kinds of birth may be found in it. What are they?
options: birth as a god, a human, a ghost, or an animal
birth from an egg, birth from a womb, birth from moisture, and birth by transformation
entering, dwelling, and emerging with awareness, or with none
infancy, childhood, youth, and middle age
quiz.why: "And four kinds of birth may be found: birth from an egg, birth from a womb, birth from moisture, and birth by transformation." A confuses the four births with the five realms (hell, animals, hungry ghosts, humans, gods), which the first half of the same sentence lists. C belongs to the four ways of entering the womb in §56; D gives four of the eight stages of life in §55.

quiz.q: Among the eight worldly conditions are 譽 and 毀, and also 稱 and 譏. According to Venerable Miào Jìng, how are the two pairs distinguished?
options: 譽 and 毀 are praise and slander behind one's back; 稱 and 譏 are praise and reproach to one's face
譽 and 毀 are spoken; 稱 and 譏 are written
譽 and 毀 concern wealth; 稱 and 譏 concern reputation
the two pairs mean the same thing, repeated for emphasis
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Praising you not to your face but behind your back is called 譽; slandering or defaming you behind your back is called 毀." "稱 and 譏: praising you to your face is called 稱, reproaching you to your face is called 譏." The Ru-Yi translation follows the same split: "praise behind one's back, blame behind one's back, praise to one's face, mockery to one's face." C is wrong: in the list, wealth is covered by "gain" and "loss." He adds that the first six are external, while suffering and pleasure are felt within — together they are the "eight winds."

quiz.q: The treatise, citing the Madhyama Āgama, lists ten kinds of those who make use of desires. Which is the tenth and highest?
options: one who seeks wealth unlawfully, but uses it, supports others, and gives in acts of merit
one who seeks wealth lawfully, uses it, supports others, gives in acts of merit — and understands renunciation in making use of it
one who seeks wealth lawfully but neither uses it, supports others, nor gives
one who seeks wealth lawfully, uses it, supports others, and gives — yet does not understand renunciation
quiz.why: The tenth: "one who seeks wealth lawfully, uses it for oneself, supports others, and gives it in acts of merit — and who does, moreover, understand renunciation in making use of it." D is the ninth, differing from the tenth only in that understanding — which Master Cháng Bǎi calls the subtlest distinction of all: even wealth lawfully gained, shared, and given can be used with unreflective attachment, or with a genuine understanding that one is not bound by it. A is the third type, C the seventh.

quiz.q: One of the four kinds of nourishment is "consciousness." How do the two teachers understand it?
options: the pursuit of knowledge through study
the eye-consciousness seeing food
the mental consciousness's hope
the sustaining hold of the ālayavijñāna — beyond solid food, contact, and volition, it is what keeps the body alive moment to moment
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The fourth, 'consciousness as food,' refers to the ālayavijñāna. Even with solid food, contact, and volition, there must still be the ālayavijñāna's sustaining hold." Master Cháng Bǎi likewise names the last of the four as "the sustaining consciousness itself." C is "volition as food," which Venerable Miào Jìng glosses as having hope — a practitioner who knows that noble ones attain the forbearance of non-arising has hope, and so keeps going.
